unit_index.interpretation: Quotienting by coordinate change converts many presentations into one arithmetic object, while an invariant polynomial supplies the correct complexity gauge. Representation type can then be read uniformly from the fixed symmetry group.

unit_index.source_title: Families of L-Functions and their Symmetry
unit_index.unit_title: Classical modular forms separate sign equidistribution from detectable support
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: Plancherel mass at ramified primes feeds the root-number formula, while the SU(2) conjugacy-class measure supplies the indicators. The Fourier support of the test function bridges a limiting density statement to actual discrimination among symmetry types.
unit_index.interpretation: Family symmetry and functional-equation sign are related but distinct information. The support threshold is an observability threshold: below it several candidate density laws agree, so a correct statistic cannot identify which law generated it.

unit_index.source_title: Families of L-Functions and their Symmetry
unit_index.unit_title: Diophantine parameter sets can encode arbitrary recursive behavior
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: The equality fiber product bridges Boolean intersection to Diophantine geometry; the square-free-part and quadratic-character map transports arbitrary recursive behavior into an automorphic family image.
unit_index.interpretation: A controlled ambient representation can lose all statistical regularity after semantic conditioning. The obstruction is not complexity of individual L-functions but loss of a lawful parameter geometry.

unit_index.source_title: Families of L-Functions and their Symmetry
unit_index.unit_title: Regular algebraic orthogonal representations have noncritical center
unit_index.nonparaphrase_operation: The bridge runs from automorphic criticality to motivic weight and Hodge parity, then through the ℓ-adic realization and its pairing sign back to the automorphic orthogonal/symplectic classification.
unit_index.interpretation: The proof reframes an analytic admissibility question as a compatibility test among parity, duality, and pairing sign. Criticality would force a representation type excluded by the hypothesis.
